q: A candidate appears in the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 33 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He passes on speed, the prescribed speed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination being 30 words per minute
options.B: He does not pass on speed, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 35 words per minute
options.C: He does not pass, the examination being decided on marks alone and not on speed
options.D: He passes only if he secures 90 per cent marks in the Pragya examination

e: The prescribed speed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination is 30 words per minute; 33 words per minute exceeds it, so the candidate passes on speed.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 82 words per minute. As regards the prescribed speed standard, the correct position is:

options.A: He falls short, the prescribed speed being 100 words per minute
options.B: He falls short, the prescribed speed being 120 words per minute
options.C: He meets the prescribed speed standard, the prescribed speed for passing the Hindi stenography examination being 80 words per minute
options.D: He meets the prescribed speed standard only if he also attains 30 words per minute in Hindi typewriting

e: The prescribed speed for passing the Hindi stenography examination is 80 words per minute; 82 words per minute meets that standard.

q: A 38-year-old employee, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He is exempt, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory after the age of 35 years
options.B: He must undergo the training only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.C: He must undergo the training only after attaining the age of 45 years
options.D: He must undergo the training, in-service Hindi training being compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained the age of 45 years

e: In-service Hindi training is compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained 45 years of age; a 38-year-old without that knowledge must undergo it.

q: An employee aged 52 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is proposed to be nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: In-service Hindi training is compulsory for him irrespective of his age
options.B: In-service Hindi training is not compulsory for him, he having attained the age of 45 years
options.C: He must undergo the training only if his office is notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976
options.D: He must undergo the training only if he is posted in Region 'C'

e: In-service Hindi training is not compulsory for an employee who has attained 45 years of age; at 52 years he is outside the compulsory training obligation.

q: A Central Government office has a total staff strength of 200, of whom 176 have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 90 per cent or more
options.C: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 95 per cent or more
options.D: Notification is not permissible for offices located in Region 'A'

e: 176 of 200 staff is 88 per cent, above the 80 per cent proportion required for notification under Rule 10(4), so the office can be notified.

q: In a newly formed Central Government office, 72 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi, and the head of office proposes its notification. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 70 per cent or more
options.B: The office can be notified, notification depending only on the total number of staff
options.C: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: The office can be notified only with the approval of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language

e: Rule 10(4) notification requires 80 per cent or more of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi; 72 per cent is below that proportion, so the office cannot be notified.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 22,500 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 20,000 words in a year
options.B: He is eligible for consideration only if the noting was done in an office notified under Rule 10(4)
options.C: He is not eligible for consideration, the scheme applying only to noting done in Region 'A' offices
options.D: He becomes eligible for consideration for the cash award, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year

e: The minimum for the noting and drafting incentive scheme is 10,000 words of Hindi noting and drafting in a year; 22,500 words exceeds it, so the employee is eligible for consideration.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 9,200 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He becomes eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 5,000 words in a year
options.B: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year
options.C: He becomes eligible for consideration only if he repeats the performance in the following year
options.D: He is eligible only if his office is located in Region 'A'

e: Eligibility for the noting and drafting incentive scheme requires at least 10,000 words of Hindi noting and drafting in a year; 9,200 words falls just below the minimum, so the employee is not eligible.

q: A Zonal Railway office issues a notification under the Official Languages Act framework in English only, and the dealing clerk contends that a notification need not be issued bilingually. The correct position is:

options.A: The contention is not correct; a notification is among the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 which must be issued in both Hindi and English, the responsibility resting with the officer signing the document
options.B: The contention is correct, notifications being outside Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.C: The contention is correct if the notification is issued in Region 'C'
options.D: The contention is correct if a Hindi version is supplied later on demand

e: A notification is a document specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 and must be issued in both Hindi and English; the signing officer is responsible for ensuring this.

q: A Ministry of the Central Government has to correspond with its attached and subordinate offices situated in Region 'A'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, such communications shall be in Hindi:

options.A: Only when the subordinate office demands it in writing
options.C: In such proportion as the Central Government may determine from time to time
options.D: In no case, English alone being prescribed for such communications

e: Under Rule 3 of the Official Language Rules, communications from a Ministry to its attached and subordinate offices in Region A are to be in Hindi in such proportion as the Central Government may determine from time to time.

q: An employee has passed the Matriculation examination with Hindi as one of the subjects. On that ground, under the Official Language Rules, 1976, he shall be deemed to have acquired:

options.A: Working knowledge of Hindi only, and not proficiency in Hindi
options.B: Neither working knowledge nor proficiency in Hindi
options.C: Both proficiency and working knowledge, but only after passing Pragya

e: Under the Rules, passing Matriculation with Hindi as one of the subjects gives working knowledge of Hindi only; proficiency requires Hindi as the medium of examination or a higher prescribed standard.

q: An employee of a Central Government office, who has not passed any prescribed Hindi examination, submits a declaration that he is in possession of working knowledge of Hindi. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: The declaration has no effect, working knowledge being recognisable only through the Pragya examination
options.B: He shall be deemed to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi, a declaration by the employee to that effect being one of the prescribed grounds
options.C: He shall be deemed to have acquired proficiency in Hindi
options.D: The declaration is valid only if he is a native of a Region 'A' State

e: Under the Rules, an employee declaration that he possesses working knowledge of Hindi is itself a prescribed ground for deeming him to have acquired working knowledge, even without passing an examination.

q: A Central Government office has been notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976. An employee of that office, who has acquired working knowledge of Hindi, contends that he can never be required to do noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: The contention is not correct; in a notified office, such an employee can be required to do noting and drafting in Hindi on the subjects specified in the notification
options.B: The contention is correct, noting and drafting remaining entirely at the choice of the employee in all cases
options.C: The contention is correct if the office is located in Region 'B'
options.D: The contention is not correct only during Hindi Pakhwada

e: In an office notified under Rule 10(4), an employee with working knowledge of Hindi can be required to do noting and drafting in Hindi on the subjects specified in the notification; the work is not left wholly to his choice.

q: In a State, the Governor, with the previous consent of the President, has authorised the use of Hindi in the proceedings of the High Court under Article 348(2) of the Constitution. A judge proposes to deliver a judgment in Hindi on the strength of that authorisation alone. The correct position is:

options.A: The judgment may be delivered in Hindi, the authorisation extending to all court work
options.B: The judgment may be delivered in Hindi if the Registrar certifies it
options.C: The authorisation does not extend to any judgment, decree or order passed or made by the High Court
options.D: The judgment may be delivered in Hindi only in Region 'A' States

e: The Governor authorisation under Article 348(2), given with the President previous consent, covers High Court proceedings but expressly does not extend to any judgment, decree or order of the High Court.

q: A citizen wishes to submit a representation for the redress of a grievance to an authority of a State in a language used in that State, other than its official language. Under Article 350 of the Constitution, the correct position is:

options.A: The representation can be submitted in Hindi only
options.B: The representation can be submitted in English only
options.C: The representation can be submitted only in the official language of the State concerned
options.D: Every person is entitled to submit such a representation in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be

e: Article 350 entitles every person to submit a representation for redress of a grievance to any Union or State authority in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee) was set up in the year 1967.
2. The Vice-Chairman of the Kendriya Hindi Samiti is the Union Home Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: the Kendriya Hindi Samiti was set up in 1967, and its Vice-Chairman is the Union Home Minister, the Prime Minister being its Chairman.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Hindi Training Institute, New Delhi was established in the year 1985.
2. The Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations under the Hindi Teaching Scheme are conducted by the Central Hindi Training Institute.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: the Central Hindi Training Institute at New Delhi was established in 1985, and the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations under the Hindi Teaching Scheme are conducted by it.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau) was set up in the year 1971.
2. The headquarters of the Central Translation Bureau is located at New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: the Central Translation Bureau, or Kendriya Anuvad Bureau, was set up in 1971 and its headquarters is at New Delhi.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi) at Agra was established in the year 1960.
2. The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct: the Kendriya Hindi Sansthan at Agra was established in 1960. It functions under the Ministry of Education, not the Ministry of Home Affairs, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the senior-most Central Government officer (head of office) in the town, nominated for the purpose.
2. The Divisional Official Language Implementation Committee of a Railway Division is chaired by the Divisional Railway Manager.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: a Town Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the senior-most Central Government head of office in the town nominated for the purpose, and a Divisional committee is chaired by the Divisional Railway Manager.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chairman of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves.
2. The secretariat of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is provided by the Department of Official Language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: the Chairman of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves, and its secretariat is provided by the Department of Official Language.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Second World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1976 at Port Louis (Mauritius).
2. The World Hindi Secretariat (Vishwa Hindi Sachivalaya) has its headquarters in Mauritius.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: the Second World Hindi Conference was held in 1976 at Port Louis in Mauritius, and the World Hindi Secretariat has its headquarters in Mauritius.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Sindhi language was included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution by the Constitution (21st Amendment) Act, 1967.
2. With the inclusion of Sindhi in the year 1967, the total number of languages included in the Eighth Schedule rose to 18.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct: Sindhi was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 21st Amendment Act of 1967. That raised the total from 14 to 15 languages, not to 18, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Languages Act, 1963 is Act No. 19 of 1963.
2. The first Official Language Commission (Kher Commission) was appointed by the President on 7th June, 1955.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: the Official Languages Act, 1963 is Act No. 19 of 1963, and the first Official Language Commission under B. G. Kher was appointed by the President on 7 June 1955.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The three-language formula for school education was first recommended by the Education Commission (Kothari Commission), 1964-66.
2. The three-language formula was adopted as a part of the National Policy on Education, 1968.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: the three-language formula was first recommended by the Education Commission of 1964-66, the Kothari Commission, and was adopted in the National Policy on Education, 1968.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 29 of the Constitution guarantees to any section of the citizens having a distinct language, script or culture of its own, the right to conserve the same.
2. Article 394A of the Constitution, which provides for the authoritative text of the Constitution in the Hindi language, was inserted by the Constitution (58th Amendment) Act, 1987.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: Article 29 protects the right of a section of citizens to conserve its distinct language, script or culture, and Article 394A on the authoritative Hindi text of the Constitution was inserted by the 58th Amendment Act, 1987.

q: A clerk who has completed the Pragya course wishes to join the Hindi typewriting and Hindi stenography classes run for Central Government employees. Such training in Hindi typewriting and Hindi stenography, besides the Hindi language courses, is provided under:

options.A: A translation training programme of the Central Translation Bureau
options.B: The correspondence courses of the Central Hindi Directorate
options.D: The Annual Programme of the Department of Official Language alone, there being no scheme for it

e: Training in Hindi typewriting and Hindi stenography, along with the Hindi language courses for Central Government employees, is provided under the Hindi Teaching Scheme.

q: An officer of a Regional Implementation Office of the Department of Official Language visits a Central Government office located in his region. The main purpose of such visits by the Regional Implementation Offices is:

options.A: To translate the codes and manuals of the office visited
options.B: To monitor and inspect the implementation of the Official Language Policy in the Central Government offices located in their respective regions
options.C: To conduct the Hindi examinations of the employees of the office visited
options.D: To print bilingual forms and stationery for the office visited

e: Regional Implementation Offices of the Department of Official Language visit Central Government offices in their regions to monitor and inspect implementation of the Official Language Policy there.

q: At the beginning of a new financial year, the head of a Central Government office asks whether fresh targets for the progressive use of Hindi will apply to his office for that year also. The Annual Programme containing such targets is issued by the Department of Official Language:

options.D: Only when the Committee of Parliament on Official Language so recommends

e: The Annual Programme laying down targets for the progressive use of Hindi is issued by the Department of Official Language every year.

q: In a Rajbhasha quiz, an employee is asked to name the first State which adopted Hindi as its official language by an Act passed in the year 1951. The correct answer is:
e: Uttar Pradesh was the first State to adopt Hindi as its official language through its Official Language Act passed in 1951.

q: An employee preparing a note records that Sanskrit is the second official language of Uttarakhand, and is asked to name the other State which has also declared Sanskrit as its second official language. The correct answer is:
e: Himachal Pradesh, besides Uttarakhand, has declared Sanskrit as its second official language.

q: An employee preparing a note on the Jammu and Kashmir Official Languages Act, 2020 has to record the number of languages declared as the official languages of the Union Territory under that Act. The correct number to be recorded is:
e: The Jammu and Kashmir Official Languages Act, 2020 declares five official languages for the Union Territory: Kashmiri, Dogri, Urdu, Hindi and English.

q: A Central Government office has to send a communication to the Government of a State which has not adopted Hindi as its official language. Under the first proviso to Section 3(1) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the language to be used for the communication is:

options.C: The regional language of that State, through an interpreter
options.D: Hindi and the regional language, in duplicate

e: The first proviso to Section 3(1) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 requires communications to a State that has not adopted Hindi as its official language to be in English.

q: Under Article 348(1) of the Constitution, until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the authoritative texts of all orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws issued under the Constitution or under any law made by Parliament or a State Legislature shall be in:

options.B: The official language of the State concerned

e: Under Article 348(1), until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the authoritative texts of all orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws issued under the Constitution or any Parliament or State law shall be in English.

q: A newly posted officer in a Railway Division asks who looks after the day-to-day work relating to the implementation of the Official Language Policy in the Division. The correct answer is:
e: In a Railway Division, the Rajbhasha Adhikari, or Official Language Officer, looks after the day-to-day work of implementing the Official Language Policy.

q: A Rajbhasha note has to record the year in which Parliament adopted the Official Language Resolution embodying the policy for the progressive use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union. The year to be recorded is:
e: The Official Language Resolution embodying the policy for the progressive use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union was adopted by Parliament in 1968.

q: An accounts office is preparing a brief history of in-service Hindi training for its Rajbhasha file. The year in which the Hindi Teaching Scheme for imparting in-service Hindi training to Central Government employees was introduced is:
e: The Hindi Teaching Scheme for in-service Hindi training of Central Government employees was introduced in 1955, following the Presidential Order on the subject.

q: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language discharges its functions through sub-committees. The number of sub-committees through which it functions is:
e: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language discharges its functions through three sub-committees, which examine offices and report to the main Committee.

q: A clerk noting the legislative history of the official language law records the date on which the Official Languages Act, 1963 received the assent of the President. The date is:
e: The Official Languages Act, 1963 received the assent of the President on 10 May 1963.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Sahitya Akademi, India's national academy of letters, was established in the year 1954.
2. The Central Institute of Indian Languages, headquartered at Mysuru, was established in the year 1969.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: the Sahitya Akademi, the national academy of letters, was established in 1954, and the Central Institute of Indian Languages at Mysuru was established in 1969.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Budget". The correct equivalent is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of the administrative term Budget, as per the official administrative glossary, is Bajat.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Scale of Pay". The correct equivalent is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of the administrative term Scale of Pay, as per the official administrative glossary, is Vetanman.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Demi-Official Letter". The correct equivalent is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Demi-Official Letter is Ardh Shaskiya Patra, ardh meaning semi or demi and shaskiya meaning official.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Competent Authority". The correct equivalent is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Competent Authority is Saksham Pradhikari, saksham conveying competence in the official administrative glossary.

q: A passenger asks at an enquiry counter in which languages 'Trains at a Glance', the All India Railway Time Table published by the Indian Railways, is published. The correct answer is:
e: Trains at a Glance, the All India Railway Time Table published by Indian Railways, is published in Hindi and English.

q: A newly posted reservation clerk is told that the passenger tickets issued by the Indian Railways are printed in:
e: Passenger tickets issued by Indian Railways are printed in Hindi and English, so that passengers of both language streams can read them.

q: A passenger reservation supervisor is checking the display arrangements at a station. The reservation charts (list of passengers) displayed at railway stations are printed in:

options.D: Three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English

e: Reservation charts displayed at railway stations are printed in three languages: the regional language, Hindi and English.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The computer-based Hindi learning package 'LILA', developed for the Department of Official Language, stands for Learning Indian Languages through Artificial Intelligence.
2. The package is a computer-based package for learning Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: LILA stands for Learning Indian Languages through Artificial Intelligence, and it is a computer-based package developed for learning Hindi.

q: A Rajbhasha note records the first province in India to adopt Hindi in the Devanagari script in place of Persian for court work, in the year 1881. That province was:
e: Bihar was the first province to adopt Hindi in the Devanagari script in place of Persian for court work, doing so in 1881.

q: At the end of the year, an office asks which authority prepares the Annual Assessment Report on the implementation of the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, which is laid before both Houses of Parliament. The report is prepared by:

options.B: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language

e: The Annual Assessment Report on implementation of the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, laid before both Houses of Parliament, is prepared by the Department of Official Language.

q: A note on linguistic minorities has to record the year in which the office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was set up. The year is:
e: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities, the Special Officer under Article 350B, was set up in 1957 to safeguard the constitutional rights of linguistic minorities.

q: An employee preparing a Rajbhasha calendar is asked in which year World Hindi Day, observed on 10th January every year, was observed for the first time. The year is:
e: World Hindi Day (Vishwa Hindi Diwas) on 10 January, marking the first World Hindi Conference of 1975, was first observed in 2006 and is celebrated annually since then.

q: A Rajbhasha quiz asks where the Third World Hindi Conference, held in the year 1983, was held. The correct answer is:
e: The Third World Hindi Conference was held in New Delhi in 1983; the first was at Nagpur in 1975 and the second at Port Louis in 1978.

q: A Rajbhasha quiz asks where the Twelfth World Hindi Conference, held in February 2023, was held. The correct answer is:
e: The Twelfth World Hindi Conference was held in February 2023 at Nadi in Fiji, continuing the practice of hosting the conference in countries with a large Hindi-speaking diaspora.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Fifth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1996 at Port of Spain (Trinidad and Tobago).
2. The Seventh World Hindi Conference was held in the year 2003 at Paramaribo (Suriname).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: the Fifth World Hindi Conference met at Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago, in 1996, and the Seventh at Paramaribo, Suriname, in 2003.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Honorarium". The correct equivalent is:
e: The standard equivalent prescribed in official glossaries for Honorarium is Maanadeya, a payment for services rendered, distinct from Paritoshik which means a reward or prize.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Superannuation". The correct equivalent is:
e: Superannuation, meaning retirement on attaining the prescribed age, is rendered as Adhivarshita; Sevanivritti is the general word for retirement.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Gazetted Officer". The correct equivalent is:
e: A Gazetted Officer is one whose appointment is notified in the Gazette, hence the standard equivalent is Rajpatrit Adhikari, Rajpatra being the Gazette.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Basic Pay". The correct equivalent is:
e: Basic Pay is rendered as Mool Vetan, meaning the core pay in the pay structure, as distinct from Vetanman, which means the scale of pay.

q: A note has to record the States in which the use of Hindi in the proceedings of the High Court has been authorised by the Governor with the previous consent of the President. The correct set of States is:

options.B: West Bengal, Odisha, Assam and Kerala
options.C: Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
options.D: Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan

e: Hindi has been authorised, with the Governor's action and the President's previous consent, for High Court proceedings in Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan.

q: An employee asks how many Official Language Commissions have been constituted under Article 344 of the Constitution so far. The correct answer is:
e: Only one Official Language Commission has been constituted under Article 344 so far, namely the commission appointed in 1955 under the chairmanship of B. G. Kher.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Manipur is placed in Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules.
2. Mizoram is placed in Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the North-Eastern States other than those placed in Region B, including Manipur and Mizoram, fall in Region C under the Official Language Rules, 1976.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Union Territory of Ladakh is placed in Region 'A' under the Official Language Rules.
2. The Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir is placed in Region 'A' under the Official Language Rules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both Union Territories, Ladakh and Jammu and Kashmir, are placed in Region A under the Official Language Rules, 1976, along with the Hindi-speaking States.

q: A note on the official language position in Goa records that, under the Official Language Act of Goa, Konkani is the official language of the State, and the language which may also be used for all or any of the official purposes of the State is:
e: Under the Goa Official Language Act, Konkani is the official language of Goa, while Marathi may also be used for all or any of the official purposes of the State.

q: An employee preparing a note on literary institutions asks in how many languages the Sahitya Akademi gives its awards for literary works. The number is:
e: The Sahitya Akademi gives its awards in 24 languages: the 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule plus English and Rajasthani.

q: A student sponsored for a Hindi programme asks where the Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya (Mahatma Gandhi International Hindi University) is located. The correct answer is:
e: The Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya, a Central University for Hindi, is located at Wardha in Maharashtra, a place closely associated with Mahatma Gandhi.

q: An office preparing its annual calendar of observances asks on which date International Mother Language Day is observed every year. The date is:
e: International Mother Language Day, proclaimed by UNESCO to promote linguistic diversity, is observed every year on 21 February.

q:
An employee compiling Census language figures for a Rajbhasha note considers the following statements:
1. In the raw returns of the Census of India, 2011, as many as 19,569 mother tongues were returned.
2. The Census of India, 2011 counts 121 languages, each spoken by 10,000 or more persons.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both figures are from Census 2011: 19,569 mother tongues were returned in the raw returns, rationalised into 121 languages each spoken by 10,000 or more persons.

q: A constitutional note has to record the Articles of the Constitution in which the Eighth Schedule is referred to. The Eighth Schedule is referred to in:
e: The Eighth Schedule is expressly referred to in Article 344, on the Official Language Commission, and Article 351, on the directive for the development of Hindi.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "House Rent Allowance". The correct equivalent is:
e: The standard equivalent of House Rent Allowance is Makan Kiraya Bhatta, the allowance paid towards the rent of residential accommodation.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Emoluments". The correct equivalent is:
e: Emoluments, meaning the total monetary benefits from employment, is rendered as Parilabdhiyan, which is wider than Vetan, meaning pay alone.

q: A Rajbhasha quiz asks in which year and from which place the first Hindi daily newspaper, 'Samachar Sudha Varshan', was published. The correct answer is:
e: Samachar Sudha Varshan, regarded as the first Hindi daily newspaper, was published in 1854 from Calcutta.

q: A Rajbhasha quiz asks where and in which year the Nagari Pracharini Sabha, founded for the promotion of the Devanagari script, was established. The correct answer is:
e: The Nagari Pracharini Sabha, founded to promote the Nagari (Devanagari) script, was established at Varanasi in 1893.

q: A Rajbhasha quiz asks who edited the first Hindi newspaper, 'Udant Martand', published from Calcutta in the year 1826. The correct answer is:
e: Udant Martand, the first Hindi newspaper published from Calcutta in 1826, was edited by Pandit Jugal Kishore Shukla.

q:
An employee verifying entries in a list of past World Hindi Conferences considers the following statements:
1. Port Louis (Mauritius) hosted the Fourth World Hindi Conference, in the year 1993.
2. Johannesburg (South Africa) hosted the Ninth World Hindi Conference, in the year 2012.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: Port Louis, Mauritius, hosted the Fourth World Hindi Conference in 1993, and Johannesburg, South Africa, hosted the Ninth in 2012.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Tenth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 2015 at Bhopal.
2. The Eleventh World Hindi Conference was held in the year 2018 at Port Louis (Mauritius).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: the Tenth World Hindi Conference was held at Bhopal in 2015 and the Eleventh at Port Louis, Mauritius, in 2018.

q: A note on classical languages records the year in which Odia was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India. The year is:
e: Odia was accorded classical language status in 2014, becoming the sixth language to receive that recognition from the Government of India.

q: After Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali were added in October 2024, the total count of languages recognised as 'classical languages' in India now stands at:
e: With Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali added in October 2024 to the earlier six, the total number of recognised classical languages stands at eleven.

q: An employee preparing a note on Hindi institutions asks in which year the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, a leading organisation for the promotion of Hindi, was founded. The year is:
e: The Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, a leading organisation for the promotion of Hindi language and literature, was founded in 1910.

q: The report of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language reaches the President under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963. The President shall cause that report to be:

options.A: Published in the Gazette of India only
options.B: Sent to the Supreme Court for its opinion
options.C: Considered by the Kendriya Hindi Samiti
options.D: Laid before each House of Parliament and sent to all the State Governments

e: Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 requires the President to cause the report of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language to be laid before each House of Parliament and sent to all State Governments.

q: A Central Government office floats a tender and prepares the tender forms and the notice inviting tenders in English only, the dealing clerk contending that tender papers are commercial documents outside the language law. The correct position is:

options.A: The contention is correct, tender forms being outside Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.B: The contention is not correct; tender forms and notices inviting tenders are among the documents specified in Section 3(3) which must be issued in both Hindi and English
options.C: The contention is correct if the tender is floated from an office located in Region 'C'
options.D: The contention is correct if a Hindi version is supplied to a bidder only on demand

e: Tender forms and notices inviting tenders are expressly listed in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, so they must be issued in both Hindi and English.

q: A Central Government office enters into an agreement with a supplier and executes it in English only, contending that agreements are private documents between the parties. The correct position is:

options.A: The contention is not correct; an agreement is among the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 which must be executed in both Hindi and English
options.B: The contention is correct, agreements being outside Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.C: The contention is correct if the supplier is a firm located in Region 'C'
options.D: The contention is correct if the agreement is kept on the file and not published

e: Agreements are among the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, so an agreement of a Central Government office must be executed in both Hindi and English.

q: A Zonal Railway headquarters issues its general orders, applicable to all divisions, in Hindi only, contending that issue in the Official Language of the Union alone is sufficient. The correct position is:

options.A: The contention is correct, general orders being outside Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.B: The contention is correct if the orders are issued from an office located in Region 'A'
options.C: The contention is not correct; general orders are among the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 which must be issued in both Hindi and English
options.D: The contention is correct if an English version is recorded on the file

e: General orders are documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 and must be issued in both Hindi and English; issue in Hindi alone is not sufficient.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Invoice". The correct equivalent is:
e: The standard equivalent of Invoice, the bill for goods supplied or services rendered, is Beejak.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Depreciation". The correct equivalent is:
e: Depreciation, the fall in the value of an asset through wear and use, is rendered as Mulya Hras, literally decrease in value.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Assets". The correct equivalent is:
e: Assets, the property and resources owned, is rendered as Parisampatti, as distinct from Deyata, which means liabilities.

q: An instructor in a Hindi workshop is asked about the level of the Praveen course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The standard of the Praveen course corresponds broadly to the Hindi standard of:
e: In the Hindi Teaching Scheme, Praveen is the middle course and its standard corresponds broadly to the middle, Class VIII, level of Hindi; Pragya corresponds to matriculation.

q: A Central Government office is finalising the purchase of books for its office library for the year. Under the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, at least what proportion of the amount spent on purchase of books for the library should be spent on Hindi books?
e: The Annual Programme target requires at least 50 per cent of the amount spent on purchase of books for office libraries to be spent on Hindi books.

q: A newly posted assistant asks in which language the Gazette of India is published. The correct answer is:
e: The Gazette of India is published in both Hindi and English, the two languages being used for official publications of the Union.

q: A Rajbhasha note on the official languages of the States has to record the official language of the State of Karnataka. The correct entry is:
e: Kannada is the official language of Karnataka, the State formed on the basis of the Kannada language.

q: A Rajbhasha note on the official languages of the States has to record the official language of the State of Punjab. The correct entry is:
e: Punjabi is the official language of Punjab under the State's official language law.

q: A litigant asks in which language the subordinate (district) courts in the State of Uttar Pradesh conduct their work. The correct answer is:
e: The subordinate or district courts in Uttar Pradesh conduct their work in Hindi, the official language used in the State's lower courts.

q:
A Rajbhasha note on the North-Eastern States considers the following statements:
1. English is the official language of the State of Nagaland.
2. English is the official language of the State of Meghalaya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: English is the official language of Nagaland and also the official language of Meghalaya.

q: In a Rajbhasha quiz, an employee is asked to name the first language to be declared a 'classical language' by the Government of India. The correct answer is:
e: Tamil was the first language declared a classical language by the Government of India, in 2004, on meeting the prescribed criteria of antiquity and literary tradition.

q: An employee verifying entries in a list of past World Hindi Conferences is asked where the Eighth World Hindi Conference, held in the year 2007, was held. The correct answer is:
e: The Eighth World Hindi Conference, held in 2007, took place at New York in the United States of America.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Liabilities". The correct equivalent is:
e: Liabilities, the amounts owed by an organisation, is rendered as Deyata, the counterpart of Parisampatti, meaning assets.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Licence". The correct equivalent is:
e: The standard equivalent of Licence is Anugyapti, a formal permission granted by a competent authority.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Consolidated Fund". The correct equivalent is:
e: The Consolidated Fund is rendered as Sanchit Nidhi, the fund into which all revenues and loans of the Government are credited under Article 266.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Contingency Fund". The correct equivalent is:
e: The Contingency Fund, kept for unforeseen expenditure, is rendered as Aakasmikta Nidhi, distinct from Sanchit Nidhi, the Consolidated Fund.

q: A note on the official language position in Goa has to record the year in which the Official Language Act of Goa, under which Konkani was declared the official language of the State, was enacted. The year to be recorded is:
e: The Official Language Act of Goa, under which Konkani in the Devanagari script was declared the official language of the State, was enacted in 1987.
